communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Haunani-Kay Trask (October 3, 1949 – July 3, 2021)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records mentioning, relating to, or generated as a result of investigation or inquiry into Professor Haunani-Kay Trask (October 3, 1949 – July 3, 2021). Her death is widely-known and widely reported; as such, privacy concerns under FOIA Exemptions 6 and 7 are voided, as are any concerns under the Privacy Act. For example, you may find her New York Times obituary at the following link: https://www.nytimes.com/2021/07/09/us/haunani-kay-trask-dead.html

Please conduct a search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Indices, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records of both HQ and all field offices for all relevant names, agencies, organizations, companies and events including but not limited to those cited in the previous paragraphs and/or links as well as a cross-reference with the Southern Poverty Law Center to include any information provided by the SPLC. My request includes but is not limited to 137, 157, 176, 177, 183, 184, 188, and 214 files. If previously released records are available, then I request a rolling release consisting of those records while additional records are located and processed for release.

If any part of these documents are exempt from disclosure, please be sure to review and release all reasonably segregable nonexempt portions of responsive documents, as the FOIA requires.

I request that I be properly classified as a media requester. I am an assistant editor at Reason Magazine who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

title: CPRA Request: Flock Safety ALPR Records

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: CPRA Request: Flock Safety ALPR Records
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Please provide copies of the following records from January 1, 2024, to the date of this request, unless a different timeframe is specified below:

I. Contracts, Funding, and Acquisition
Please provide documents for Items 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 from the period between the inception of the agency's relationship with Flock Group, Inc. (Flock Safety) and the present.
1. All contracts, licensing agreements, software-as-a-service (SaaS) subscriptions, Master Services Agreements (MSA), and Memoranda of Understanding (MOU) between the San Bruno Police Department (or the City of San Bruno acting on its behalf) and Flock Group, Inc. (Flock Safety).
2. Any amendments, renewals, extensions, or change orders to the agreements described in Item 1.
3. All purchase orders, invoices, and records of payments made to Flock Safety.
4. Records identifying the specific funding sources used for these systems (e.g., General Fund, asset forfeiture funds, state/federal grants, or private donations).
5. All internal memos, proposals, or staff reports discussing the acquisition, approval, placement, or pilot programs for Flock ALPR cameras.

II. Policy, Privacy, and Governance
6. The current ALPR Usage and Privacy Policy, as required by California Civil Code § 1798.90.51, including data retention schedules and access protocols.
7. Annual ALPR audit reports required by Civil Code § 1798.90.53.
8. Training materials, policies, or directives provided to sworn and civilian personnel regarding authorized use of the Flock system.
9. Any Surveillance Use Policies, Anticipated Surveillance Impact Reports, or Privacy Impact Assessments related to ALPR technology generally or Flock Safety specifically.
10. The San Bruno Police Department's records about agendas, minutes, or logs of meetings regarding the contracting, implementation, or security of Flock Safety cameras.
11. Documentation regarding public notification of surveillance, including signage standards, maps provided to the public, or press releases.
12. Any complaints or grievances received from the public regarding ALPR camera placement or data use.

III. Operational and Technical Data
13. A list of all current and planned locations of Flock Safety ALPR cameras deployed by the San Bruno Police Department (including those in unincorporated areas and contract cities), including: coordinates or intersection descriptions, installation dates, the specific purpose for each location (e.g., traffic monitoring, crime prevention), camera model numbers/hardware specifications.
14. The names and titles of the specific System Administrators or managers responsible for the oversight of the Flock Safety system (e.g., Professional Services Division Commander).

IV. Usage Data, Sharing, and Audits
15. The total number of license plates scanned (read) by the San Bruno Police Department's Flock cameras, aggregated by month.
16. All existing audit or access logs generated by the Flock Safety system documenting queries/searches conducted by agency personnel. I request that personally identifiable information of non-employee subjects be redacted rather than the records withheld. Please include: date and time of search, reason for search (as entered into the system audit trail), and the agency or unit of the officer conducting the search.
17. Records regarding the sharing of ALPR data with the Northern California Regional Intelligence Center (NCRIC), including but not limited to: 
- Any MOUs, data-sharing agreements, or network-participation terms governing the transmission of the San Bruno Police Department's ALPR data to NCRIC; 
- Records describing the technical mechanism by which data is shared (e.g., automatic real-time feed, batch upload, or query-based access);
- Any policies, directives, or written guidance governing what restrictions, if any, the San Bruno Police Department places on NCRIC's downstream use or further dissemination of San Bruno Police Department-origin ALPR data;
- Records of any requests received from NCRIC (or through NCRIC from other agencies) to query or obtain San Bruno Police Department ALPR data, and the San Bruno Police Department's responses to such requests.
18. A list of all "hot lists" (e.g., stolen vehicles, Amber alerts) or custom "hot lists" currently integrated into the San Bruno Police Department Flock system.
19. A list of all outside agencies (local, state, and federal) that the San Bruno Police Department shares Flock data with, and a list of all outside agencies from whom the San Bruno Police Department receives Flock data, including but not limited to access provided through Flock Safety's real-time network sharing features (e.g., the platform previously known as TALON), and any data-sharing agreements, MOUs, or network participation terms governing such access.
20. Any statistical reports or evaluations generated by the department or Flock Safety regarding the efficacy of the system (e.g., number of vehicles recovered, arrests made attributable to ALPR hits).
21. Records of any unauthorized access, data breaches, or security incidents involving ALPR data.

V. Communication
22. All written communications (emails and attachments) between San Bruno Police Department employees and representatives of Flock Safety (email domain @flocksafety.com), excluding routine IT troubleshooting tickets.
23. All written communications with other law enforcement agencies or federal partners regarding requests to access or share San Bruno Police Department Flock data.

If you determine that any portion of the requested records is exempt from disclosure, please redact only those portions and provide the remainder of the record. For any redaction or denial, please cite the specific legal exemption justifying the withholding, as required by Government Code § 7922.540.

Given that this request is made in the public interest by a student journalist writing for Scot Scoop, I respectfully request a waiver or reduction of any fees associated with this request.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Maximus Kwan

communications.subject: RE: California Public Records Act Request: CPRA Request: Flock Safety ALPR Records
communications.communication:
Dear MuckRock News,

The City received your Public Records Act (PRA) request via email on February 17, 2026, requesting that the City produce:

I. Contracts, Funding, and Acquisition
Please provide documents for Items 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 from the period between the inception of the agency's relationship with Flock Group, Inc. (Flock Safety) and the present.
1. All contracts, licensing agreements, software-as-a-service (SaaS) subscriptions, Master Services Agreements (MSA), and Memoranda of Understanding (MOU) between the San Bruno Police Department (or the City of San Bruno acting on its behalf) and Flock Group, Inc. (Flock Safety).
2. Any amendments, renewals, extensions, or change orders to the agreements described in Item 1.
3. All purchase orders, invoices, and records of payments made to Flock Safety.
4. Records identifying the specific funding sources used for these systems (e.g., General Fund, asset forfeiture funds, state/federal grants, or private donations).
5. All internal memos, proposals, or staff reports discussing the acquisition, approval, placement, or pilot programs for Flock ALPR cameras.

II. Policy, Privacy, and Governance
6. The current ALPR Usage and Privacy Policy, as required by California Civil Code § 1798.90.51, including data retention schedules and access protocols.
7. Annual ALPR audit reports required by Civil Code § 1798.90.53.
8. Training materials, policies, or directives provided to sworn and civilian personnel regarding authorized use of the Flock system.
9. Any Surveillance Use Policies, Anticipated Surveillance Impact Reports, or Privacy Impact Assessments related to ALPR technology generally or Flock Safety specifically.
10. The San Bruno Police Department's records about agendas, minutes, or logs of meetings regarding the contracting, implementation, or security of Flock Safety cameras.
11. Documentation regarding public notification of surveillance, including signage standards, maps provided to the public, or press releases.
12. Any complaints or grievances received from the public regarding ALPR camera placement or data use.

III. Operational and Technical Data
13. A list of all current and planned locations of Flock Safety ALPR cameras deployed by the San Bruno Police Department (including those in unincorporated areas and contract cities), including: coordinates or intersection descriptions, installation dates, the specific purpose for each location (e.g., traffic monitoring, crime prevention), camera model numbers/hardware specifications.
14. The names and titles of the specific System Administrators or managers responsible for the oversight of the Flock Safety system (e.g., Professional Services Division Commander).

IV. Usage Data, Sharing, and Audits
15. The total number of license plates scanned (read) by the San Bruno Police Department's Flock cameras, aggregated by month.
16. All existing audit or access logs generated by the Flock Safety system documenting queries/searches conducted by agency personnel. I request that personally identifiable information of non-employee subjects be redacted rather than the records withheld. Please include: date and time of search, reason for search (as entered into the system audit trail), and the agency or unit of the officer conducting the search.
17. Records regarding the sharing of ALPR data with the Northern California Regional Intelligence Center (NCRIC), including but not limited to:
- Any MOUs, data-sharing agreements, or network-participation terms governing the transmission of the San Bruno Police Department's ALPR data to NCRIC;
- Records describing the technical mechanism by which data is shared (e.g., automatic real-time feed, batch upload, or query-based access);
- Any policies, directives, or written guidance governing what restrictions, if any, the San Bruno Police Department places on NCRIC's downstream use or further dissemination of San Bruno Police Department-origin ALPR data;
- Records of any requests received from NCRIC (or through NCRIC from other agencies) to query or obtain San Bruno Police Department ALPR data, and the San Bruno Police Department's responses to such requests.
18. A list of all "hot lists" (e.g., stolen vehicles, Amber alerts) or custom "hot lists" currently integrated into the San Bruno Police Department Flock system.
19. A list of all outside agencies (local, state, and federal) that the San Bruno Police Department shares Flock data with, and a list of all outside agencies from whom the San Bruno Police Department receives Flock data, including but not limited to access provided through Flock Safety's real-time network sharing features (e.g., the platform previously known as TALON), and any data-sharing agreements, MOUs, or network participation terms governing such access.
20. Any statistical reports or evaluations generated by the department or Flock Safety regarding the efficacy of the system (e.g., number of vehicles recovered, arrests made attributable to ALPR hits).
21. Records of any unauthorized access, data breaches, or security incidents involving ALPR data.

V. Communication
22. All written communications (emails and attachments) between San Bruno Police Department employees and representatives of Flock Safety (email domain @flocksafety.com), excluding routine IT troubleshooting tickets.
23. All written communications with other law enforcement agencies or federal partners regarding requests to access or share San Bruno Police Department Flock data.
from January 1, 2024 to present.

The City continues to review documents to determine if any of the records are exempt from disclosure.  We estimate that we will be able to provide additional responsive records on or before October 1, 2026.  If we require additional time, we will let you know as soon as possible.  As always, the City’s goal is to comply promptly with any such requests and we will endeavor to respond earlier if possible.  Thank you.

Sincerely,


[A drawing of a cartoon character  Description automatically generated]
Lupita Huerta, CMC
City Clerk
City of San Bruno
567 El Camino Real
San Bruno, CA  94066
(650) 616-7061 [office]
(650) 616-7070 [direct] / lhuerta@sanbruno.ca.gov<mailto:lhuerta@sanbruno.ca.gov>

*NOTE:  The City Clerk’s Office workweek schedule is
Monday through Thursday, 7:30 am to 5:30 pm.

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Public Records Request: Peregrine (Folsom Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

- A copy of all training materials, including but not limited to any handouts, workbooks, assessments, presentations, slides, videos, audio files, or other materials, either developed in-house or provided to the agency pertaining to the agency's use of Peregrine products.
- A copy of all agency manuals either developed in-house or provided to the agency pertaining to the agency's use of Peregrine products.
- A copy of all agency policies and procedures either developed in-house or provided to the agency pertaining to the agency's use of Peregrine products.
- A roster of all agency employees who either have a user account for Peregrine products or have internal agency permissions to use Peregrine products as of today
- A roster of all agency employees who have completed agency training for the use of Peregrine products as of today
- Documents sufficient to show all user accounts for the department’s Peregrine deployment that were active between 1/1/2024 and the date that this request is processed.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Joey Scott

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Abraham Harold Maslow (April 1, 1908 – June 8, 1970) - renowned American psychologist who was best known for creating "Maslow's hierarchy of needs" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Maslow).

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

File Numbers: 100-BS-30168

Sincerely,

J Ader

communications.communication:
Thank you for contacting foipaquestions@fbi.gov.  Please check the status of your FOIPA Request at http://vault.fbi.gov by clicking on “Check Status of Your FOI/PA Request” on the right side of the page, and follow the instructions below.

Check the Status of Your FOIPA Request
If your FOIPA Number is [1234567-0] please enter [1234567-000] into the system. If your FOIPA Number is [1234567-1] please enter [1234567-001] into the system. If you have any questions about the status of your FOIPA request, please e-mail foipaquestions@ic.fbi.gov.

FIND STATUS OF FOIPA- Request statuses are updated weekly

Please enter the whole FOIPA number-Example: [1234567-000]

FOIPA:
Results will show the Request Number, Case Type and Process Description shown below:
FOIPA:
1234567-000

Case Type:
FOIPA

Process Description (Will display the current progress of the request)
The FBI’s FOIPA Program is searching the FBI’s indices for potentially responsive documents.
You may be contacted via formal letter for all fees and/or negotiation issues that may apply.

NOTE: Recent requests are entered into the FOIPA database in the order that they are received. Before you can check the status, you must have received correspondence assigning a FOIPA request number and the information transferred to the online database. Status information is updated weekly. If a request has been closed within the last six months the online database will display the following: The FOIPA number entered has been closed, and appropriate correspondence has been sent to the address on file.

Estimated Dates of Completion
Requests are processed in the order in which they are received through our multi-track processing system.  Requests are divided into two primary tracks--simple (under 50 pages of potentially responsive documents) and complex (over 50 pages of potentially responsive documents).  Complex requests are further divided into medium, large, and extra-large sub-tracks based upon request size.  Simple track requests typically require the least amount of time to process.  Currently, simple track cases average approximately 138 days from the date of receipt for processing.  Our complex requests in the medium processing track are currently averaging 571 days, large processing track are currently averaging approximately 1,289 days, and extra-large processing track are currently averaging 1,649 days for processing.

Respectfully,

Public Information Officer

170 Marcel Drive
Winchester, VA  22602

E: foipaquestions@fbi.gov<mailto:foipaquestions@fbi.gov>

Please check the status of your request online at https://vault.fbi.gov/fdps-1/@@search-fdps    Status updates are performed on a weekly basis.

Note:  This is a non-emergency email address.  If this is an emergency, please call 911 directly.  If you need to report a tip for immediate action, please contact FBI Tips at http://tips.fbi.gov/ or reach out to your local field office.

communications.subject: Re: Status request - RF-122 / RD 64263
communications.communication:
Dear J Ader:

You requested a status update on *RD 64263*, a request our office received 
on July 13, 2020 and to which we initially replied on August 28, 2020. The 
request was assigned to our Tier 1 processing queue for review.

To give you an indication of our existing backlog for cases in Tier 1, 
there are approximately 816 cases ahead of yours. Unfortunately, the 
COVID-19 pandemic has created many unprecedented challenges in our work. 
The majority of the records that our customers request require our staff to 
be on-site to search for and review microfilm, microfiche, or original 
textual records. Staffing levels on-site have been severely limited with 
long periods where our facility was closed. Even as we expand our 
reopening, operations may be temporarily curtailed due to limited staffing 
and/or deteriorating local health conditions.

Our small staff has and will continue to work diligently to process each 
request as quickly as possible.

Please note, we will not respond to status update requests more than once 
every six months.

To notify this office of a change in your contact information or to track 
the status of your request, please telephone 301-837-3190 or e-mail 
specialaccess_foia@nara.gov. If you have specific questions regarding the 
subject of your request, please contact Stephanie Coon directly at 
stephanie.coon@nara.gov or 301-837-1604. All communications concerning this 
request should reference your case tracking number *RD* *64263*.

Sincerely,

Ashney Randle
Government Information Specialist
Special Access & FOIA Program (RF)
National Archives at College Park

communications.subject: National Archives FOIA RD 64263
communications.communication:
Dear J. Ader,

I am writing in further response to your Freedom of Information Act request
of July 13, 2020 for records in the custody of the National Archives and
Records Administration. Your request for FBI case files 100-BS-30168 and
100-HQ-415677 on Abraham Maslow was received in this office on August 24,
2020 and assigned FOIA tracking number RD 64263.

Your request is nearing the front of our processing queue. Before we begin
processing your request, we want to verify your current contact information
and confirm that you are still interested in the records.

You may contact us by email at specialaccess_foia@nara.gov. If we do not
hear from you within 90 calendar days from the date of this letter, your
FOIA request will be administratively closed.

If you are not satisfied with my action on this request, you have the right
to file an administrative appeal within ninety (90) calendar days from the
date of this letter. Appeals must be in writing and may be delivered by

title: Flock Safety ALPR Use Across Union County, NJ — Camera Locations, Audit Logs, Searches & Data Sharing (Union County Prosecutor’s Office)

communications.subject: New Jersey Open Public Records Act Request: Flock Safety ALPR Use Across Union County, NJ — Camera Locations, Audit Logs, Searches & Data Sharing (Union County Prosecutor’s Office)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New Jersey Open Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

This request is directed specifically to the Union County Prosecutor’s Office (“UCPO”), not the Union County Sheriff’s Office.

On August 25, 2026, Lieutenant Michael Richards of the Plainfield Police Department advised me in writing that the Flock Safety cameras installed throughout the City of Plainfield are owned and maintained by UCPO and that Plainfield Police personnel have access to those cameras.

Accordingly, I request the following existing government records maintained by or for UCPO:

A. CAMERA INVENTORY AND LOCATIONS

1. The current inventory, deployment list, device list, site list, spreadsheet, database export, report, map, or other existing record identifying every Flock Safety ALPR camera owned, leased, funded, administered, maintained, or operated by UCPO, including cameras located in Plainfield and elsewhere in Union County.

For each camera, please provide all location-related fields maintained in the record, including, where available:

- Camera, device, or site name and identification number;
- Municipality;
- Street address, nearest address, intersection, roadway, road segment, or block;
- Latitude and longitude or other geographic coordinates;
- Installation or activation date;
- Whether the camera is active, inactive, relocated, or removed; and
- The public entity or other organization funding or hosting the camera.

2. Existing maps, GIS files, KML/KMZ files, spreadsheets, site plans, installation records, deployment records, work orders, permits, or similar records showing the locations of UCPO’s Flock Safety cameras.

If UCPO asserts that precise coordinates or particular site details are exempt, please provide the reasonably segregable remainder, including at minimum the municipality, roadway, nearest intersection or block, and number of cameras at each location, and identify the specific legal authority supporting each redaction.

B. AGREEMENTS, PROCUREMENT, ACCESS, AND DATA SHARING

3. All currently effective contracts, order forms, statements of work, amendments, renewals, memoranda of understanding, and agreements concerning UCPO’s acquisition, ownership, installation, operation, administration, maintenance, or use of Flock Safety cameras, software, data, or services.

4. Purchase orders, invoices, quotes, proposals, requisitions, payment records, and other procurement records associated with UCPO’s current Flock Safety deployment and current contract term.

5. Currently effective agreements, memoranda, arrangements, or other records concerning Flock Safety camera ownership, funding, hosting, access, or data sharing between UCPO and:

- Municipal police departments;
- County, state, federal, or other law-enforcement agencies;
- Public entities;
- Homeowner associations;
- Private businesses;
- Private organizations; or
- Individuals.

6. Existing lists, reports, exports, screenshots, or configuration records identifying:

- Every agency or organization authorized to access data from Flock Safety cameras owned, maintained, or administered by UCPO;
- Every agency or organization whose Flock Safety data is accessible to UCPO;
- Every Flock Safety network joined or administered by UCPO; and
- UCPO’s current network-sharing configuration and access permissions.

7. The names of all hot lists, watch lists, alert lists, or comparable lists currently enabled, used, or accessible within UCPO’s Flock Safety account. This item seeks the names or categories of the lists and does not seek the underlying license-plate entries.

C. USAGE AND AUDIT RECORDS

For the period July 20, 2026 through August 19, 2026:

8. Existing reports showing the aggregate number of vehicle detections or license-plate reads captured by Flock Safety cameras owned, maintained, or administered by UCPO. This item seeks aggregate statistics and does not seek photographs or an unredacted database of individual license plates.

9. All Organization Audit reports, Network Audit reports, audit logs, search logs, query logs, usage reports, administrative reports, or equivalent exports reflecting UCPO’s use or administration of Flock Safety during the requested period, including existing fields showing:

- Dates and timestamps of searches or queries;
- Usernames, user IDs, badge numbers, agency names, or other user-identification fields;
- Reasons, justification categories, case numbers, or incident numbers associated with searches, where maintained;
- Networks or agencies searched;
- Changes to users, permissions, hot lists, alerts, cameras, or network-sharing settings;
- Changes to data-sharing relationships or network access; and
- Live-view, live-stream, camera-access, or comparable permissions and configuration changes.

10. Existing reports or exports from Flock Safety’s Insights section, or any equivalent reporting feature, concerning camera usage, searches, detections, network access, or data sharing during the requested period.

For Item 9, UCPO may redact license-plate numbers, vehicle photographs, or case-specific information that it determines is lawfully exempt. I nevertheless request disclosure of all reasonably segregable administrative information, including dates, times, agency identifiers, user identifiers, action types, justification categories, and configuration changes.

FORMAT AND SEARCH INSTRUCTIONS

This request seeks existing government records and does not require UCPO to conduct research or create a new record. If a requested list does not exist as a standalone record, please provide the existing database export, spreadsheet, report, map, audit log, configuration record, screenshot, installation record, or other record containing the requested information.

Please provide records in their original electronic or native format where reasonably available. I prefer:

- CSV, XLS, XLSX, or another machine-readable format for inventories, logs, and reports;
- KML, KMZ, GeoJSON, shapefile, or another native GIS format for location data; and
- Searchable PDF or native document format for contracts and related documents.

If any portion of a responsive record is withheld, please redact only the exempt information, disclose the reasonably segregable remainder, and identify the specific statutory authority and explanation for each withholding or redaction.

If another Union County office physically maintains responsive records on UCPO’s behalf, please route this request appropriately while continuing to treat UCPO as the agency whose records are requested.

CERTIFICATIONS

Under penalty of N.J.S.A. 2C:28-3, I certify that:

1. I HAVE NOT been convicted of any indictable offense under the laws of New Jersey, another state, or the United States.

2. I, or another person, WILL NOT use the requested government records for a commercial purpose.

3. I AM NOT seeking these records in connection with a legal proceeding.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Madthew Pierre-Louis

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: Itemized Fee Petitions, Invoices, and Settlement Payouts (McMinimee Law)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. All itemized invoices, line-item billing sheets, and fee petitions submitted to Vancouver Public Schools, its legal counsel, its board of directors, or its risk-management carriers by Shannon McMinimee or any agent operating under the domain or entity name "McMinimee Law".
2. All transactional records, ledger entries, checks, voucher approvals, board warrant registry items, or electronic funds transfer records documenting attorney fee payouts, cost reimbursements, or financial settlement distributions paid directly to McMinimee Law or Shannon McMinimee, specifically including but not limited to the $9,000.00 check/warrant processed on or around March 10, 2026 under Account Code 10 E 530 9700.
3. The chronological scope of this request spans from January 4, 2022, through June 30, 2025, specifically targeting all billing blocks, settlement agreements, and fee recovery actions generated while the attorney was concurrently operating under private credentials and public employment contracts.

PRE-EMPTIVE STATUTORY ENFORCEMENT & COMPLIANCE CLAUSE:

communications.subject: RE: Washington Public Records Act Request #R001116-080326
communications.communication:
Dear Jen Anderson,

Thank you for the general ledger entries provided on August 31, 2026. While the District has provided basic accounting records proving Check No. 415420 was processed, the response remains non-compliant with the full scope of the request under the Washington Public Records Act (PRA). I object to the administrative closure of this request based on the following deficiencies:

1. Item 1 (Line-Item Billing Sheets): Page 19 contains only a flat summary sheet referencing a block of 30.0 hours. Under Progressive Animal Welfare Society (PAWS) v. University of Washington, 125 Wash. 2d 243 (1994), attorney billing sheets and time blocks documenting public expenditures are public records subject to disclosure. Please produce the actual itemized time logs, dates, and detailed line-item billing entries submitted by McMinimee Law to justify the $10,500 total expenditure.

2. Item 2 (Over-Redaction of Settlement Agreement): Pages 8, 9, and 10 of the produced settlement contract are entirely blacked out. Under Soter v. Cowles Publishing Co., 162 Wash. 2d 716 (2007) and RCW 42.56.210(1), blanket page-level withholdings are structurally unlawful. While the District must redact specific student-identifiable elements protected by FERPA, it is legally required to segment the record, leaving the systemic contractual terms, general operational agreements, and non-identifiable text fully visible. 

Please provide a revised, properly parsed production of the settlement agreement and the missing detailed time logs to satisfy this request.

Respectfully Submitted in the Public Interest,

Public Interest Mainstreaming Parenting

You may file a request with NARA using the address above.  Please reference file numbers 100-HQ-454082 Serials 4, 6, 24, and 5; 100-HQ-454549 Serial 4-P17, 32, 42, 6-P16; 100-HQ-455596, 100-HQ-456482 Serial 9; 100-HQ-461197 Serial 13 and 2; 100-NY-166899, 62-HQ-117964 Serial 164, 88-HQ-49004 Serial 118, 76 89, 90, 91, 97, 77, 113, 145, 130, 186, and 166; 100-BS-46975 Serial 10; 100-BS-47199 Serial 1; and 100-AL-21998 Serial 435 in your correspondence."

Sincerely,

J Ader

communications.subject: Fwd: FOIA Request Deletion: NARA-NGC-2020-000447
communications.communication:
Dear Mr. Ader:

Thank you for submitting your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to
the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA), via the
*FOIAOnline* website.  We received your request on March 16, 2020.  Your
request concerns FBI files.

Our office uses the *FOIAonline* portal for FOIA and Privacy Act requests
for the National Archives and Records Administration's *operational* records
(records created by this agency).  Your *FOIAOnline *request is for records
that may be *archival* records (records created by or originated in a
different agency but that may have been transferred to the legal custody of
NARA), to which access is restricted. Therefore, we have forwarded it to
our *Office of Research Services, Special Access and FOIA* (RF) staff who
handle FOIA requests for such archival records.

Since *Research Services* does not process FOIA requests through
*FOIAOnline*, we removed your request from the *FOIAOnline* website.  *Special
Access *staff will assign you a new tracking number, and respond directly
to you. In the future, if you need to follow up with that office directly,
please contact them at the address below, or electronically via email.

The National Archives and Records Administration
Special Access and FOIA Staff (RF)
8601 Adelphi Road, Room 5500
College Park, MD 20740

By phone: 301-837-3190
By fax: 301-837-1864
By email: specialaccess_foia@nara.gov

For your reference, a copy of your request with one attachment is below.

Please visit our website at www.archives.gov/foia for further information
about submitting a FOIA request to NARA.  On our main website,
www.archives.gov, you can learn more about the resources we offer to the
public, and you can access our online catalog.

Thank you for contacting the National Archives.

Sincerely,
Susan Gillett
Government Information Specialist
Office of General Counsel
National Archives and Records Administration
College Park, MD 20740-6001
301-837-3409
susan.gillett@nara.gov

communications.communication:
Dear Mr. Ader,



I am writing in response to your Freedom of Information Act request of
March 16, 2020 for records in the custody of the National Archives and
Records Administration. Your request was received in this office on March
17th and assigned FOIA case number RD 64052.

within case files, and individual page numbers within serials, each
identified by the FBI as potentially responsive to your request for records
relating to Murray Bookchin.

Because I have determined that FBI case file number 100-HQ-454082 ends with
serial number 2, I am denying *only* this portion of your request on
procedural grounds. However, if you believe that 100-HQ-454082 is
responsive to your request, please contact me directly at
christopher.abraham@nara.gov or 301-837-2958 within ninety (90) calendar
days from the date of this letter. If we do not hear from you within ninety
(90) calendar days, we will administratively close* only *the portion of
your case relating to 100-HQ-454082.



All of the remaining materials require screening for categories of
information exempted from disclosure under the terms of the FOIA, prior to
public release. In particular, there are documents that may be redacted to
protect the identities of confidential sources, including FBI informant
codes and informant file numbers.



Collectively, the responsive materials in your request amount to
approximately 235 pages. Requests for FBI case files that do not exceed 700
pages are assigned to our first-tier processing queue. Taking into
consideration our existing backlog, the estimated time required to complete
the processing of your request is approximately 30 months from the date of
this letter.



Please note that once we have notified you that review is complete, you may
either visit our College Park, MD facility to view the file at no cost or
order a reproduction. You may order a reproduction copy at the cost of
$0.80 per page by contacting our office to place an order. We estimate that
the cost of a reproduction will be $188.00.

communications.subject: Re: FOIA Case No. RD 64052 re Multiple FBI Records Concerning Murray Bookchin
communications.communication:
Dear Sir -



I contacted the FBI on your behalf concerning the outstanding issues
on 62-HQ-117964 and 100-HQ-454082 . As I indicated in my email of March
23rd, I was unable to locate 62-HQ-117964 in its entirety and unable to
locate 100-HQ-454082 serials 4-6 and 24 during the allotted search time. As
a final search tactic, I contacted FBI on your behalf about these two
issues and have just today received a response.


*62-HQ-117964* - FBI indicates it still has 62-HQ-117964  in its
possession. Therefore, I recommend that you contact the FBI directly (
https://www.fbi.gov/services/records-management/foipa) if you wish to
request it.




*100-HQ-454082 serials 4-6 and 24* - FBI concurs with the National Archives
that the case was transferred here, but cannot give an accounting of the
serial numbers within it. As you will recall from my email of the 23rd, we
only have serials 1 and 2 for this case file. Therefore, this portion of
your request remains denied on procedural grounds as previously outlined.
Regardless,if you believe that this file is still responsive to your
request, please see the instructions included in my email of the 23rd to
keep it an active portion of the request.


Sincerely,


*Chris Abraham*
Archivist
Special Access and FOIA Branch (RF)
301.837.2958
www.archives.gov/research/foia/

communications.communication:
February 19, 2026

Dear Mr. Ader,

I am writing in further response to your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA)
request RD 64052 for records in the custody of the National Archives and
Records Administration.

Some of the records you requested have been reviewed for another requester
(RD 61316). Please be advised, we have considered the foreseeable harm
standard when reviewing records and applying FOIA exemptions for this
request. Information was released to the greatest extent possible. Below is
a summary of our review:

You requested access to  FBI case file numbers: 100-HQ-454549 Serial 4 and
Serial 6, 100-HQ-455596, 100-HQ-456482 Serial 9, 100-HQ-461197 Serials 2
and 13, 100-NY-166899, 100-BS-47199 Serial 1, and 100-AL-21998 Serial 435.
These files have been reviewed for another requestor.

You requested 88-HQ-49004 serials 76, 77, 89, 90, 91, 97, 113, 118, 130,
145, 166, 186 which are still in the processing queue.

You requested 100-BS-46975, currently only Serial 10 of 100-BS-46975 has
been reviewed for another requestor, the remaining file is still in the
queue.

I completed a line-by-line review of the records you requested. Please be
advised, I have considered the foreseeable harm standard when reviewing
records and applying FOIA exemptions for this request. Information was
released to the greatest extent possible. Below is a summary of my review:

Part Pages
Withheld in Full

100-NY-166899 126 108 18 0

100-BS-47199 Serial 1 2 1 1 0
100-AL-21998 Serial 435 4 4 0 0

I withheld information protected under section (b) of the FOIA (5 U.S.C.
552). The specific reasons for the denials are:

TYPE OF INFORMATION WITHHELD

FOIA EXEMPTION or STATUTE

classified national security information

(b)(1)

privileged or confidential trade secrets and commercial or financial
information

(b)(4)

personal privacy of living individuals

(b)(6)

identities of confidential sources

(b)(7)(D)

You or your designated representative may view the file(s) at the National
Archives at College Park, Maryland. We require at least one week advance
notice to prepare for your visit and ask that you email
specialaccess_foia@nara.gov with the FOIA tracking number of the previous
requestor (RD 61316) as well as your FOIA tracking number (RD 64052) and
the date you plan to visit. Please monitor our web page
https://www.archives.gov/college-park for details and updates, as the
operating status for the facility could change, affecting opening hours for
the research rooms.

If you cannot visit our College Park facility, you may order a digital or

It is possible the fees to hire a researcher may be less than the

researcher to duplicate the file, information on how to hire a researcher

National Archives does not endorse anyone who appears on the list

If you are not satisfied with my action on this request, you have the right
to file an administrative appeal within ninety (90) calendar days from the

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Complaints to Blue Ash (Department of Homeland Security Office of Inspector General)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

On behalf of my client, Ohio Immigrant Alliance:

For the ICE Blue Ash Field Office, since 2020;

1. All closed JIC complaints or communications that were created; and,
2. Subsequent investigative reports.


I request expedited processing of this request pursuant to 6 CFR 5.5(e) and state under penalty of perjury pursuant to 28 USC 1746 that these records are a matter of widespread interest (federal enforcement of immigration laws and the conduct of ICE officials) and about which there exist serious questions of government wrongdoing and public safety. Moreover, my client, Ohio Immigrant Alliance disseminates information about immigration enforcement activities. See https://www.ohioimmigrant.org, especially the drop-down boxes on the home page titled "News" and "Multimedia." There is an urgent need to inform the public about the extent to which complaints related to this office have been substantiated and the corrective measures were recommended.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Lara S Nochomovitz

See https://www.ohioimmigrant.org, especially the drop-down boxes on the home page titled "News" and "Multimedia." There is an urgent need to inform the public about the extent to which complaints related to this office have been substantiated and the corrective measures were recommended.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Lara S Nochomovitz

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: City of Oakland March 4 Rejection Letters
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. March 2026 claim rejection letters. All letters, notices, or other written communications issued by or on behalf of the City of Oakland during the period March 1, 2026 through March 31, 2026, inclusive, that reject, deny, return as untimely, return as insufficient, or otherwise dispose of a claim for money or damages presented to the City under the Government Claims Act (Gov. Code, § 900 et seq.). This includes documents titled "Notice of Rejection," "Notice of Insufficiency," "Notice of Untimeliness," "Notice of Return of Claim," and any equivalent form letter, regardless of the title used.

2. The March 4, 2026 letters specifically. Without limiting Item 1, all such letters issued on or about March 4, 2026 on claims arising out of the City's closure of, and enforcement action at, the E. 12th Street median encampment.

3. Transmittal records. For each letter responsive to Items 1 and 2, the transmittal record showing the date the letter was mailed, emailed, or otherwise served and the address or addresses to which it was sent (including cover letters, mailing logs, proof-of-service forms, certified mail receipts, or email transmittal messages).

4. Claim log or register. Any claim log, register, spreadsheet, database export, or tracking report identifying claims presented to the City that were rejected, returned, or otherwise disposed of in March 2026, showing at minimum the claim number, claimant name, date of claim, date of disposition, and disposition type. A report or export generated from the City's existing claims-tracking system is acceptable and is not the creation of a new record where the system can produce it in the ordinary course.

5. Council or delegated-authority action. Any City Council agenda item, resolution, staff report, or delegated-authority determination approving or authorizing the rejection of the claims described in Items 1 and 2.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robbie Powelson

communications.subject: The Missouri Sunshine Law Request: ALPR audit
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the The Missouri Sunshine Law, I hereby request the following records:

Concerning Flock Safety, these files;

1. Organization Audit in Flock.
The report should include data logged from the period of January 1, 2025, to the date this request is processed. Per Flock's documentation, the Organization Audit is available within the Insights tab and is defined as searches done within the agency.

2. Network Audit in Flock.
The report should include data logged from the period of January 1, 2025, to the date this request is processed. Per Flock's documentation, the Network Audit is available within the Insights tab and is defined as searches of the organization’s Flock network by any agency in the Flock System.

Typically the output for these audits is available in monthly batches.

3. A list of network share settings that include:
3a. Flock networks shared with me
3b. Networks that I’m sharing

4. All contracts concerning purchasing and installation for Flock Safety

Please provide records in their original electronic, machine readable format. For example, please provide csv or spreadsheet files where applicable.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Kansas City DSA

communications.communication:
In response to your request for items 3 through 4, attached is the City’s contract with Flock Safety. I have also included a link to the Blue Springs Police Department’s Flock Safety Transparency Portal:
https://transparency.flocksafety.com/blue-springs-mo-pd

The transparency portal provides access to our applicable policy and identifies the agencies or entities with which data may be shared. There are no individual data-sharing agreements between agencies. Data sharing is elective and is determined by each agency utilizing the Flock Safety system.
Additional Police Department policies and information are available through the City of Blue Springs website.
Regarding Questions 1 and 2, Missouri law requires a governmental body to produce existing public records; however, it does not require a governmental body to create a new record or compile information that does not already exist in response to a records request. See Weeks v. St. Louis County, 696 S.W.3d 333 (Mo. banc 2024), and Jones v. Jackson County Circuit Court, 162 S.W.3d 53, 60 (Mo. App. W.D. 2005). Answering questions 1 and 2 would create a new record as described above.

communications.subject: North Carolina Public Records Law Request: Jail Booking Log / Arrest Register (Jan 2025-present)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the North Carolina Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

Under the North Carolina Public Records Law, N.C. Gen. Stat. § 132-1 et seq., I request the following existing record: The daily jail booking log (booking register / arrest blotter) for all individuals booked into your facility from January 1, 2025 through the present. For each booking, I request the fields your booking system already records: (1) name of the individual booked; (2) date and time of booking; (3) the charge(s) and offense level; (4) bond amount and type, and the date any bond was posted; and (5) the date and manner of release from your custody. This is routine booking data maintained in your jail-management system in the ordinary course. I will accept it in whatever native electronic format your system exports (a spreadsheet or delimited file is ideal; I do not require a formatted report). As a public-interest, non-commercial request, I ask for a fee waiver or reduction; if any fee is anticipated, please provide an itemized written estimate before incurring cost. Please preserve all responsive records pending completion.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

communications.subject: Indiana Access to Public Records Act Request: Noah Pyke (Howard County Sheriff)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Indiana Access to Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records related to the following current or former employees:

Noah Pyke (3630-0418)

Hiring date, termination date, compensation, commendations, assignments/job roles, disciplinary actions, factual basis for disciplinary actions and letters of resignation for the following employees. Please exclude copies of individual training certificates.

I am including the following information as a helpful reference to related case law and Public Access Counselor opinions regarding personnel records of public employees:

https://public.courts.in.gov/Decisions/api/Document/Opinion?Id=QPNIyLTvnhzxDZhO52J1KCEs4fPOKpLR0hAitsADZUhV--IpFNWE224Cxiw0N3jJ0

Indiana Supreme Court decision WTHR-TV v. Hamilton Southeastern School District states that APRA requires disclosure of the factual basis for disciplinary action, and that factual basis cannot be a bald conclusion. It also has to be sufficient for a reasonable person to understand what an employee did to deserve discipline. See the opinion starting on page 7 of the link above.

A passing reference to violation of a specific policy is not sufficient to meet this standard.

The Indiana Public Access Counselor also has addressed the topic of resignations in lieu of termination. One such opinion can be reviewed here, but simply put a resignation in lieu of a termination does not dissolve an agency’s responsibility to provide the factual basis for discipline under the public records statute.

The state’s records statute applies to all employees, regardless of wither they are probationary or not.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Emily Hopkins

records for the requested time frame of September 21, 2025, through

“Flock” and “Flock Safety,” as well as emails sent to or received from

attached for your review. These records constitute the responsive email
records located within the possession and control of the Brookfield Police
Department. Responsive email threads and available attachments have been
included where applicable.

With regard to the portion of your Missouri Sunshine Law request concerning
records of the North Missouri Drug Task Force, including the Drug Task
Force Officer's email records, please be advised that the Brookfield Police
Department does not maintain or house records of the North Missouri Drug
Task Force and does not have access to the Drug Task Force Officer's email
records.

to designate a custodian of records who is responsible for the maintenance
of that governmental body's records. Because the Brookfield Police
Department does not maintain or have access to the North Missouri Drug Task
Force's email records, those records are not within the possession or
control of the Brookfield Police Department and cannot be produced by this
department.

communications.subject: RE: Freedom of Information Act Request #FA-24-1166 / FP-24-009065
communications.communication:
To whom it may concern,

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:
1. All email records from base commanders from 2016 to 2017 containing the terms "pokemon," "Pokemon GO" or "Niantic"
2. All email records between the Army and The United States Department of Defense from 2016 to 2017 containing the term "pokemon"
3. All internal memos or training documents regarding personal cellphone use on Army property from 2016 and 2017
4. All notices to Army staff from 2016 to 2017 containing the terms "pokemon" "Pokemon GO" or "Niantic"

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Sincerely,

Brianna Cluck

title: Uranium One Deal (U.S. Department of State)

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Uranium One Deal (U.S. Department of State)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

According to the Treasury Department, CFIUS gathers on a weekly basis to discuss pending transactions.  Please provide all records related to each meeting discussing Uranium One/Rosatom to include all transcripts, memoranda, and other communications regarding the transaction.

Please provide all records relating to the criminal and intelligence investigation into senior managers of Tenex, Tenam, and Rosatom prior to CFIUS approval of the Uranium One transaction in October 2010.

Please provide a copy of all records related to the presentation provided by Uranium One/Rosatom to CFIUS staffers prior to filing a formal notice on August 4, 2010.

Please provide a copy of your agency’s official confirmation to Treasury that the transaction did not raise any unresolved national security concerns.

Please provide all records relating to your agency’s determination that the Uranium One/Rosatom transaction did not raise any unresolved national security concerns.

Please provide all records relating to communications with respect to Secretary Clinton and donations to the Clinton Foundation by parties interested in the Uranium One/Rosatom transaction.

Please provide all records referencing Uranium One, Atomredmetzoloto (ARMZ), Rosatom, Tenex, Tenam, Ian Telfer, Vadim Mikerin, Rennaisance Capital, Igor Sagiryan, Prevezon Holdings, Canada, European Union, Mark Lambert, Transport Logistics International Inc. (TLI), between 2004 and 2018 referring to the Uranium One Deal.

All documents, including communications, relating to interactions between the NRC and the DOE with regard to the 2010 transfer of control of Uranium One to ARMZ and the 2013 purchase of the remaining interests in Uranium One.

All documents, including communications, relating to each export and subsequent transfer of natural uranium produced in the U.S. by Uranium One following the transfer of control of the company to ARMZ in 2010.

All documents, including communications relating to your agency’s determinations that the sale of Uranium One, exports of its uranium, and subsequent transfers between foreign countries did not raise any unresolved national security concerns.

All documents, including communications, relating to your agency’s recommendation to President Obama to resubmit the U.S.-Russia 123 agreement for peaceful nuclear cooperation to Congress for review.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Andrew Klum

Dear Lancaster County Clerk:

Pursuant to the Nebraska Public Records Act, Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 84-712 through 84-712.09, I request copies of the following existing records maintained by the Lancaster County Clerk, the Board of Commissioners, or in County Board agenda, minute, contract, financial, or legislative files.

Please search for records created, received, or maintained from January 1, 2018 through the date this request is processed using the terms: ALPR, LPR, “automatic license plate reader,” “automated license plate reader,” “license plate recognition,” “license plate reader,” “plate reader,” Axon, Motorola, Flock, “state highway right-of-way,” and “Department of Transportation.”

Please provide:

All County Board agendas, agenda packets, minutes, resolutions, motions, public presentations, staff reports, exhibits, meeting recordings or links, and correspondence concerning ALPR/LPR systems, services, data, deployment, funding, policy, privacy, or interagency access.

All executed contracts, interlocal agreements, memoranda of understanding, statements of work, amendments, renewals, purchase orders, procurement records, bids, proposals, sole-source justifications, invoices, payment vouchers, claims, grant records, and budget records concerning ALPR/LPR systems or services.

All agreements and supporting materials involving the Nebraska Department of Transportation and the installation, operation, maintenance, or removal of ALPR/LPR equipment on state highway right-of-way, including all amendments, site maps, correspondence, approvals, and related County Board records.

All records concerning the County’s procurement, approval, funding, operation, or oversight of Motorola, Axon, Flock, or any other ALPR/LPR vendor or contractor.

All County Board or Clerk records concerning ALPR/LPR policies, privacy policies, retention practices, audits, public complaints, legal analyses, risk assessments, data-sharing arrangements, or reporting under Neb. Rev. Stat. § 60-3206.

All records showing payments, approved expenditures, appropriations, grant funds, reimbursement requests, or recurring costs for ALPR/LPR programs, including equipment, installation, software, subscription, cloud-storage, mobile-data, support, or maintenance costs.

This request does not seek raw captured plate data, individual license plate numbers, raw ALPR images, or other data excluded from public disclosure by Neb. Rev. Stat. § 60-3209.

Please provide responsive records electronically by email or download link. Please provide spreadsheets and other structured records in their native or reasonably accessible machine-readable format where maintained in that form.

I am a Nebraska resident. Please notify me before incurring fees exceeding $50. If you estimate greater costs, please provide an itemized estimate and identify the highest-cost categories so I can prioritize or narrow the request.

If another County office is the custodian of responsive records, please identify that office or forward the request as appropriate. If any responsive material is withheld or redacted, please identify the specific statutory basis and release all reasonably segregable non-exempt information.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 4 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jeff Geiger

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Expedited FOIA Request NARA 22-V.D.MUCK. NARA FOIA Instructions and SOPs
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

(FYSA. FOIA Join the fight for FOIA compliance. FOIAcomplaince@gmail.com)

Expedited FOIA Request NARA 22-V.D.MUCK. NARA FOIA Instructions and SOPs. [See PDF for full FOIA Request]

I am respectfully seeking via Muckrock.com:
1.	NARA’s current FOIA regulation.

NARA’s 2022 Chief FOIA Officer Report states:
3. The FOIA Improvement Act of 2016 required all agencies to update their FOIA regulations within 180 days. In 2016, OIP issued Guidance for Agency FOIA Regulations and the accompanying Template for Agency FOIA Regulations to assist agencies in updating their regulations in accordance with the statute. Has your agency updated its FOIA regulations in accordance with the FOIA Improvement Act of 2016? If 
not, what is your agency's plan to update your regulations?
Answer: Yes. However, NARA is preparing to update our regulations in light of new 
Supreme Court rulings on exemptions

2.	NARA’s FOIA Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for operational records FOIA requests (FOIAonline identifies NARA Operational Records)

NARA’s 2022 Chief FOIA Officer Report states:
Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) generally document your agency’s internal processes for administering the FOIA beyond your FOIA regulations and FOIA Reference Guide. As noted in OIP’s guidance, having SOPs can improve the consistency and quality of an agency’s FOIA process. SOPs can also serve as a significant resource for incoming FOIA professionals and a way to preserve much of the agency’s institutional knowledge on administering the FOIA from how to handle requests from start-to finish, to identifying and making proactive disclosures, to maintaining a FOIA website. Does your agency have up-to-date internal SOPs for your FOIA administration? Answer: Yes. NARA’s offices that process FOIA requests have separate SOPs. Each office reviews their SOPs on an annual basis.

3.	I am also seeking a copy of this FOIA Request, which is an Agency record that exists and is in the Agency’s possession at the time of my FOIA request. This record is a responsive record integral to my Request. Release of the Agency’s copy is not optional.
4.	See PDF for complete FOIA Request. See Requested Format.
5.	Although I am seeking expedited processing and prompt release of all records, I am seeking a rolling release of those records that are immediately available followed by a list of additional searches and estimated completion dates for them.

REQUESTED FORMAT. 
I am seeking a PDF file with thru MUCKROCK.com with: (1) a signed and dated cover letter (citing my personally assigned requester control number); (2) with record page count for all records released records (3) a copy of this request in your reply. I seek records in this format with an imbedded copy of my requests to (1) impede the agency from not addressing the FOIA Request; (2) impede the Agency from not providing the documents stated in the Agency’s letter reply, and (3) make it obvious in any subsequent review what the Agency has or has not done. 

Further, I request that these records be sent in any digital formats in which they exist (such as PDF and Excel). Under the terms of the E-FOIA Amendments of 1996, Section 5, if a document exists in electronic format, it must be released in that format upon request.

Each record must be provided as a distinct record in their native format. 
I am also seeking the “Description Available to the Public” field in FOIAonline be set to yes and that all records be released to and viewable in the application by the general Public. The release type must be set to “Unredacted – Releasable to the General Public: Will be available to the general public,” or to “Redacted – Releasable to the General Public: Will be available to the general public.”

This request is distinctly separate from any other. Please do not combine this request with any other request in your reply. I am requesting that each element of the records sought be specifically addressed in the reply.

EXPEDITED PROCESSING. 
I am seeking expedited processing. In any denial of my request for expedited processing the Agency must state in detail how my request does not meet requirement and who, by name, was involved in the denial determination.
1.	The  subject is of widespread and exceptional media interest and the information sought involves possible questions about the government's integrity that affect public confidence. 
a.	The next and final FOIA Advisory Committee of the 2020 – 2022 Term is June 9, 2022, where this matter will be discussed. This is the final term of this committee
b.	Based on records released regarding individualized tracking numbers, status and estimated completion dates of my FOIA requests and appeals, NARA may be engaging in massive false FOIA reporting. There can be no dispute  that such matters are the subject of widespread and exceptional media interest and the information sought involves possible questions about the government's integrity that affect public confidence.
c.	Please refer further to my FOIA Public Comments regarding the March 29, 2022 Senate Oversight Committee FOIA Hearings, wherein DOJ OIP and NARA’s OGIS were slammed for lack of FOIA compliance oversight. 
d.	I plan to distribute information from this expedited FOIA request to members of the media and others via a vast distribution network.
e.	I am an individual primarily engaged in dissemination of information via extensive email lists, blogs, coordination with Open Government Advocate Organizations and members of the media.

2.	Information is urgently needed to inform the public concerning some actual or alleged government activity/malfeasance. 
a.	See paragraph 1 above incorporated fully herein..
b.	I am recognized within to FOIA Advisory Committee Recommendation “OGIS 2.0: Reimagining FOIA Oversight” dated 05.04.2022 as an expert contributor “Robert (Bob) Hammond, Citizen FOIA Advocate.”
3.	In any denial of expedited processing, NARA must repeat each paragraph and sub-paragraph above and state explicitly how my request does not meet the cited standards. A blanket statement without doing so lacks required content.

In any denial of my request for expedited processing, I am seeking that the Agency identify who, by name and email was consulted and that the Agency provide specific justification  as to how my request stated herein does not qualify.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Hammond
